hyde.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
hyde.description: Adversaries may exploit vulnerabilities in applications exposed to the Internet, including by injecting database commands through user-supplied input. They may do so to gain unauthorized access, execute code, or obtain access to underlying systems.

hyde.name: Web Shell
hyde.description: Adversaries may place a web shell on a publicly accessible server to execute commands remotely through web requests. They may use web shells to maintain access, perform follow-on actions, and interact with the compromised host.

hyde.name: Application Shimming
hyde.description: Adversaries may create or modify application compatibility shims to redirect the execution of legitimate programs to malicious code. They may use this mechanism to establish persistence and execute code when applications or the operating system starts.

hyde.name: Valid Accounts
hyde.description: Adversaries may use legitimate credentials, including compromised accounts with elevated privileges, to access servers that manage organizational users and resources. They may abuse these accounts to blend in with normal activity and obtain broader access within an environment.

hyde.name: Network Service Scanning
hyde.description: Adversaries may scan a network to identify active hosts, available services, and systems that could be targeted for further access. They may use the results to map the environment and select additional hosts for lateral movement.

hyde.name: System Information Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may collect information about a compromised computer, such as its operating system, hardware, configuration, and installed software. They may use this information to understand the host and determine which follow-on actions are likely to succeed.

hyde.name: Screen Capture
hyde.description: Adversaries may capture screenshots from a compromised computer using operating system functions or dedicated tools. They may collect screenshots to obtain sensitive information displayed on the screen and monitor user activity.

hyde.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
hyde.description: Adversaries may send collected information to an external system through an established command and control channel. They may use this channel to transfer host details, screenshots, and other data while reducing the need for a separate exfiltration mechanism.

hyde.name: OS Credential Dumping
hyde.description: Adversaries may extract account credentials, including password hashes, from system memory or other operating system stores. They may use these credentials to obtain access to additional systems or accounts without knowing the original passwords.

hyde.name: Pass the Hash
hyde.description: Adversaries may authenticate to systems using stolen password hashes instead of the corresponding plaintext passwords. They may use this technique to access privileged accounts and move laterally within an environment.

hyde.name: Valid Accounts
hyde.description: Adversaries may use legitimate accounts, including accounts with administrative privileges, to access management interfaces and enterprise resources. They may abuse these accounts to blend malicious activity with normal authenticated access.

hyde.name: Account Access Removal
hyde.description: Adversaries may change passwords or otherwise modify account access controls to prevent legitimate users from accessing systems and resources. They may use this technique to disrupt operations and maintain control over compromised environments.

hyde.name: External Proxy
hyde.description: Adversaries may install or use software that routes connections through an external service or intermediary. They may use external proxies to establish outbound access, conceal the origin of traffic, or maintain a communication path to compromised systems.

hyde.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
hyde.description: Adversaries may transfer collected data through an established command and control channel. They may use this channel to avoid creating a separate communications path for exfiltration.

hyde.name: SSH
hyde.description: Adversaries may use Secure Shell to remotely access systems and execute commands. They may authenticate with valid accounts or stolen credentials to administer multiple systems and move laterally.

hyde.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt data on systems or network shares to interrupt availability and prevent legitimate users from accessing it. They may encrypt files across multiple systems to disrupt operations and demand recovery actions.

hyde.name: External Remote Services
hyde.description: Adversaries may access internal systems through external-facing remote services using valid credentials or other authentication mechanisms. They may use these services to establish an initial foothold or maintain access while bypassing internal network boundaries.

hyde.name: Spearphishing Attachment
hyde.description: Adversaries may send targeted emails containing malicious attachments to induce recipients to open or execute them. The attachments may deliver malware, exploit vulnerabilities, or establish access to the recipient’s system.

hyde.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
hyde.description: Adversaries may exploit vulnerabilities in applications or services exposed to the internet, including unpatched email or web servers. They may use successful exploitation to gain unauthorized access, execute code, or establish persistence within the environment.

hyde.name: Process Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may enumerate running processes on a system to identify applications, services, and security tools. This information may help them understand the environment and select processes to evade, terminate, or abuse.

hyde.name: Impair Defenses
hyde.description: Adversaries may disable or modify security tools, backup software, logging, or other defensive mechanisms. They may do so to reduce the likelihood of detection, prevent recovery, or allow subsequent malicious actions to proceed without interference.

hyde.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt data on targeted systems or network shares to prevent access by legitimate users. They may use encryption to disrupt operations and coerce victims into meeting demands for restoration.

hyde.name: Spearphishing Attachment
hyde.description: Adversaries may send phishing emails containing malicious attachments that masquerade as legitimate documents, often using trusted themes or senders to appear credible. The attachments are intended to deliver malware or induce users to execute malicious content.

hyde.name: Malicious File
hyde.description: Adversaries may rely on users to open a malicious file delivered through email or other means. Opening the file can execute embedded scripts or other payloads, enabling further compromise of the system.

hyde.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
hyde.description: Adversaries may establish persistence by adding programs or scripts to Registry Run Keys or Startup folders. These locations cause the specified content to execute automatically when a user logs on or the system starts.

hyde.name: System Information Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may gather information about operating systems and computer identities, such as the hostname and OS version. This information can help them identify systems, tailor subsequent actions, and track compromised hosts.

hyde.name: Software Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may enumerate installed software and applications on a system. This information can help identify security tools, exploitable software, and other capabilities available on the host.

hyde.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
hyde.description: Adversaries may send collected system information to an adversary-controlled command and control channel. Using the existing channel allows them to transfer reconnaissance data and receive further instructions while reducing the need for a separate communication path.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system to a compromised host. They may use web requests, remote services, or other transfer mechanisms to stage malware for execution.

hyde.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
hyde.description: Adversaries may execute downloaded binaries through command shells, scripting interpreters, or other command-line mechanisms. This enables them to run tools and payloads on compromised systems.

hyde.name: Credentials from Web Browsers
hyde.description: Adversaries may search browser profile directories and credential stores for saved account information. They may decrypt or extract stored usernames, passwords, cookies, and other authentication data for unauthorized access.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer

hyde.name: Keylogging

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may transfer backdoor files or other tools to a compromised system using network services, scripts, or installation mechanisms. This enables them to deploy capabilities needed for persistence, execution, or command and control.

hyde.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
hyde.description: Adversaries may establish persistence by adding programs to Registry Run Keys or Startup Folders. These programs are executed automatically when a user logs on or the system starts.

hyde.name: Masquerading
hyde.description: Adversaries may disguise malicious files by using names, locations, or attributes that resemble legitimate software or system components. This can mislead users and security tools into treating the files as benign.

hyde.name: Web Service
hyde.description: Adversaries may use popular web services or messaging platforms to communicate with compromised systems and issue commands. Using legitimate services can help blend command and control traffic with normal network activity.

hyde.name: Encrypted Channel
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt command and control traffic using protocols such as HTTPS or other encrypted communication mechanisms. Encryption helps protect commands and data from interception and reduces the visibility of network communications.

hyde.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
hyde.description: Adversaries may obfuscate command and control data or other content through encoding, byte manipulation, encryption, or similar transformations. This can hinder analysis and help evade content-based detection mechanisms.

hyde.name: System Information Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may query system information to identify the operating system, hostname, hardware configuration, and other characteristics of a compromised device. This information can help them tailor subsequent actions and determine the capabilities of the environment.

hyde.name: Process Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may enumerate running processes to identify active applications, security tools, services, and other processes on a compromised device. This information can help them assess the environment, evade detection, and select processes for further interaction.

hyde.name: LSASS Memory

hyde.name: Shortcut Modification
hyde.description: Adversaries may modify desktop shortcut files to point to malicious executables or commands instead of the intended applications. This causes the malicious content to execute when users launch programs through the altered shortcuts.

hyde.name: Token Impersonation/Theft
hyde.description: Adversaries may steal access tokens from processes belonging to other users and impersonate those users. This enables them to execute actions with the privileges and identity associated with the stolen tokens.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer

hyde.name: Bypass User Account Control
hyde.description: Adversaries may execute scripts or other methods that bypass user account control mechanisms to obtain elevated privileges. They may do so to run processes with administrative permissions and access protected resources.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may transfer modified credential-dumping tools to a compromised system. They may stage these tools locally so they can execute them and collect authentication material.

hyde.name: OS Credential Dumping
hyde.description: Adversaries may obtain credentials by extracting authentication material from operating system stores, memory, or security databases. They may use the recovered credentials to access additional accounts, systems, or resources.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment. They may store the transferred files in prepared directories for later execution or use.

hyde.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may copy tools or other files from one compromised system to another system within the environment. They may use lateral file transfers to stage tools for execution on additional hosts.

hyde.name: Remote Services: SSH
hyde.description: Adversaries may use Secure Shell to remotely access systems with valid credentials. They may use stolen administrative passwords to establish remote sessions and perform actions on the target system.

hyde.name: Drive-by Compromise

hyde.name: External Remote Services

hyde.description: Adversaries may combine and compress collected files into an archive before exfiltration. Archiving reduces the number of files transferred and may decrease the visibility of the data transfer.

sub_queries: ตรวจสอบการเชื่อมต่อเครือข่ายที่เปิดอยู่ หมายเลขปลายทาง และพอร์ตบนเครื่อง (System Network Connections Discovery)
รวบรวมชื่อเครื่อง รุ่นระบบปฏิบัติการ และรายละเอียดการตั้งค่าของเครื่องลูกข่าย (System Information Discovery)
สอบถามความสัมพันธ์ความน่าเชื่อถือระหว่างโดเมนขององค์กรกับโดเมนอื่น (Domain Trust Discovery)
ตรวจสอบว่าบัญชีผู้ใช้บนเครื่องเป็นสมาชิกของกลุ่มสิทธิ์ใดบ้าง (Permission Groups Discovery)

hyde.name: System Network Connections Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may inspect active network connections on a compromised system, including remote addresses and ports. This information may be used to identify connected systems, services, and potential communication paths for further activity.

hyde.name: System Information Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may gather information about a compromised system, such as its hostname, operating system, hardware, and configuration details. This information may be used to identify the system and tailor subsequent actions or payloads.

hyde.name: Domain Trust Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may query domain trust relationships to identify organizational domains that are connected through established trust. This information may be used to map potential access paths and identify additional systems or environments of interest.

hyde.name: Permission Groups Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may enumerate the groups to which a user account belongs on a compromised system. This information may be used to determine the account's privileges and identify opportunities for privilege escalation or lateral movement.

sub_queries: หลอกผู้เสียหายให้ติดตั้งโปรแกรมซื้อขายสินทรัพย์ดิจิทัลปลอมบนเครื่อง macOS
ใช้ชุดคำสั่งผ่านตัวแปลคำสั่งของระบบให้ทำงานทันทีหลังติดตั้งโปรแกรม
ย้ายไฟล์ตั้งค่าไปไว้ใน Scheduled Task/Job: Launchd เพื่อให้โปรแกรมคนร้ายทำงานทุกครั้งที่เปิดเครื่อง
ตรวจสอบพารามิเตอร์ที่กำหนดไว้ก่อนเริ่มทำงาน
เก็บรวบรวมข้อมูลเจ้าของเครื่องและชื่อผู้ใช้ที่กำลังใช้งานอยู่ (System Owner/User Discovery)
เข้ารหัสข้อมูลที่รวบรวมด้วยกุญแจที่ฝังไว้ในตัวโปรแกรม
ส่งข้อมูลเจ้าของเครื่องและชื่อผู้ใช้ออกไปยังเว็บไซต์สั่งการของคนร้ายผ่านช่องทางเดียวกับที่ใช้รับคำสั่ง (Exfiltration Over C2 Channel)

hyde.name: Malicious File
hyde.description: Adversaries may persuade users to download and execute a malicious file disguised as legitimate software. This can provide an initial foothold by causing the user to run attacker-controlled code.

hyde.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
hyde.description: Adversaries may use a system command interpreter to execute commands or scripts during or immediately after software installation. This enables them to automate actions and invoke operating system functionality without directly embedding all functionality in the installer.

hyde.name: Launchd
hyde.description: Adversaries may create or modify launchd configuration files to establish persistence on macOS systems. The operating system can then automatically execute attacker-controlled programs when the system starts or when specified launch conditions occur.

hyde.name: Execution Guardrails
hyde.description: Adversaries may check predefined parameters or environmental conditions before executing malicious functionality. These checks can limit execution to intended systems or help avoid analysis and detection in unsuitable environments.

hyde.name: System Owner/User Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may enumerate the username or account associated with the current user and identify the system owner. This information can support host profiling, targeting decisions, and subsequent account-focused actions.

hyde.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt collected data using a key embedded in malicious software before storing or transmitting it. This can obscure the content from security tools and make analysis or inspection more difficult.

hyde.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
hyde.description: Adversaries may transmit collected data to an external server through the same channel used to communicate with command and control infrastructure. Using an established C2 channel can reduce the need for separate exfiltration mechanisms and help blend the transfer with routine malicious communications.

sub_queries: ลบไฟล์เครื่องมือสั่งงานเครื่องระยะไกล ไฟล์ตัวติดตั้งโปรแกรมฝังตัว และไฟล์เครื่องมือดึงรหัสผ่านออกจากเครื่องแม่ข่ายเก็บไฟล์ (Indicator Removal on Host)
โปรแกรมฝังตัวสั่งแจกแจงรายการโปรแกรมและกระบวนการที่กำลังทำงานอยู่บนเครื่อง (Process Discovery)
ค้นหากระบวนการที่ทำงานภายใต้สิทธิ์ของผู้ดูแลโดเมน
ได้มาและนำสิทธิ์ประจำตัวจากกระบวนการที่ทำงานภายใต้สิทธิ์ผู้ดูแลโดเมนไปใช้
สร้างบัญชีผู้ใช้ใหม่ในโดเมนขององค์กร (Account Manipulation)
กำหนดสิทธิ์ระดับผู้ดูแลให้บัญชีผู้ใช้ใหม่ในโดเมน
ใช้บัญชีผู้ใช้โดเมนที่มีสิทธิ์ผู้ดูแลเป็นช่องทางกลับเข้ามาในภายหลัง (Persistence)

hyde.name: Indicator Removal on Host
hyde.description: Adversaries may delete tools, installers, and other files from compromised hosts to remove evidence of their activity. They may target files used for remote access, execution, credential collection, or other operational purposes to hinder forensic analysis.

hyde.name: Process Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may enumerate running processes on a host to understand active applications, identify security software, and locate processes of interest. This information may help them select targets for credential access or privilege escalation.

hyde.name: System Owner/User Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may identify the users or accounts associated with running processes to determine whether privileged accounts are active on a host. They may use this information to target processes operating under administrative or other high-privilege contexts.

hyde.name: OS Credential Dumping
hyde.description: Adversaries may obtain credential material from memory or other operating system locations associated with privileged processes. They may use the recovered credentials to impersonate users, access additional resources, or perform actions with elevated privileges.

hyde.name: Account Manipulation
hyde.description: Adversaries may create or modify user accounts in an organization’s domain to establish access under attacker-controlled identities. They may use these accounts to maintain access or support additional actions within the environment.

hyde.name: Account Manipulation
hyde.description: Adversaries may assign administrative or other elevated privileges to accounts they control. This enables them to perform privileged actions and retain access even if other compromised credentials are invalidated.

hyde.name: Valid Accounts
hyde.description: Adversaries may use legitimate domain accounts with administrative privileges to access systems and maintain a foothold. They may rely on these accounts as a persistence mechanism because activity can appear similar to that of an authorized user.

sub_queries: สั่งให้เครื่องแม่ข่ายและเครื่องลูกข่ายเริ่มระบบใหม่เข้าสู่โหมดปลอดภัยเพื่อไม่ให้โปรแกรมรักษาความปลอดภัยโหลดทำงาน (Impair Defenses)
เข้ารหัสลับไฟล์งานบนเครื่องแม่ข่ายและเครื่องลูกข่ายด้วยอัลกอริทึมสมมาตร 256 บิตและเข้ารหัสกุญแจซ้ำด้วยกุญแจสาธารณะ 2048 บิต (Data Encrypted for Impact)
ลบข้อมูลสำรองที่เก็บไว้ในเครื่องเพื่อขัดขวางการกู้คืนข้อมูล (Inhibit System Recovery)
ปิดตัวเลือกการกู้คืนระบบตอนเริ่มเครื่องเพื่อขัดขวางการกู้คืนข้อมูล (Inhibit System Recovery)
ลบสำเนาเงาของไฟล์ทั้งหมดเพื่อขัดขวางการกู้คืนข้อมูล (Inhibit System Recovery)

hyde.name: Impair Defenses
hyde.description: Adversaries may reboot systems into a restricted operating mode in which security software and monitoring tools do not load. This can impair defensive capabilities and allow malicious activity to proceed without detection.

hyde.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt data on local and network-accessible systems using symmetric encryption and protect the encryption keys with asymmetric cryptography. This can prevent access to files and support extortion or other disruptive objectives.

hyde.name: Inhibit System Recovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may delete locally stored backups to prevent restoration of affected data. This can reduce recovery options and increase the impact of destructive or ransomware activity.

hyde.name: Inhibit System Recovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may disable system recovery options that are available during system startup. This can prevent administrators from reverting systems to an earlier operational state.

hyde.name: Inhibit System Recovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may delete volume shadow copies and other point-in-time file snapshots. This can prevent recovery of encrypted or corrupted files from locally maintained copies.

sub_queries: ควบคุมเครื่องคอมพิวเตอร์แผนกต้อนรับจากระยะไกล
บันทึกภาพหน้าจอพนักงานเป็นระยะ (Screen Capture)
สั่งให้ไฟล์โปรแกรมที่วางไว้บนเครื่องทำงานผ่าน Windows Command Shell
ตรวจสอบรายการกระบวนการที่กำลังทำงานอยู่ทั้งหมดเพื่อสำรวจสภาพแวดล้อม (Process Discovery)

hyde.name: Remote Access Software
hyde.description: Adversaries may use remote access software to control systems over a network. Such software can provide interactive access to a compromised host for execution, administration, or data collection.

hyde.name: Screen Capture
hyde.description: Adversaries may capture screenshots of a victim’s desktop or active application windows. Screen captures can be collected periodically to monitor user activity and obtain information displayed on the screen.

hyde.name: Windows Command Shell
hyde.description: Adversaries may execute commands through the Windows command shell to run programs, scripts, and other commands. This can enable execution of previously placed files and facilitate system manipulation.

hyde.name: Process Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may enumerate running processes to identify active applications, services, and security tools. This information can be used to understand the system environment and determine subsequent actions.

sub_queries: ฝังโปรแกรมควบคุมระยะไกลลงในเครื่องคอมพิวเตอร์ของเจ้าหน้าที่ระดับบริหาร
โปรแกรมฝังตัวที่ทำงานด้วยสิทธิ์ระดับระบบเรียกตัวติดตั้งของโปรแกรมฝังตัวรุ่นถัดไปขึ้นมาทำงาน
ตัวติดตั้งแก้ไขค่าในทะเบียนระบบเพื่อวางการตั้งค่าของโปรแกรมฝังตัว
โปรแกรมฝังตัวตรวจสอบชื่อบัญชีผู้ใช้ที่กำลังทำงานอยู่
ดาวน์โหลดสคริปต์เข้ามาเพื่อทำ Password Spraying
นำรหัสผ่านที่คาดเดาง่ายไปลองล็อกอินกับบัญชีผู้ดูแลโดเมนหลายบัญชี
พยายามเชื่อมต่อไดรฟ์ของเครื่องแม่ข่ายควบคุมโดเมน

hyde.name: Remote Access Software
hyde.description: Adversaries may install or deploy remote access software on a targeted system to obtain interactive control over it. They may use such software to remotely execute commands, access files, and maintain access to the system.

hyde.name: Native API
hyde.description: Adversaries may use native operating system APIs to invoke and execute additional tools, installers, or payloads from an existing process. This can allow them to perform execution while operating with the privileges of the calling process.

hyde.name: Modify Registry
hyde.description: Adversaries may modify the Windows Registry to store configuration data or alter system settings. They may use registry changes to support execution, persistence, or the operation of malicious software.

hyde.name: System Owner/User Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may query the operating system to identify the account under which a process or session is running. This information may be used to determine available privileges and guide subsequent actions.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may download scripts or other tools from a remote location to a compromised system. They may transfer these resources to obtain capabilities needed to conduct follow-on activity.

hyde.name: Password Spraying
hyde.description: Adversaries may attempt to authenticate to multiple accounts using a small number of commonly used or otherwise likely passwords. This technique is intended to avoid account lockouts while identifying accounts with weak credentials.

hyde.name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
hyde.description: Adversaries may connect to administrative shares on remote Windows systems using the Server Message Block protocol. They may use these shares to access files, move laterally, or execute actions on remote systems.

sub_queries: วางไฟล์สคริปต์ PowerShell ที่อำพรางนามสกุลเป็นไฟล์ข้อมูลธรรมดาบนเครื่องแม่ข่าย
ถอดรหัสสคริปต์ PowerShell ที่ถูกอำพราง
เรียกใช้สคริปต์ PowerShell อีกชั้นที่ถูกอำพราง
ใช้เทคนิค DLL Side-Loading หลอกโปรแกรมที่ถูกต้องให้เรียกไฟล์ DLL ของคนร้าย
อำพรางเนื้อหาสคริปต์ PowerShell เพื่อซ่อนคำสั่งติดต่อเครื่องสั่งการ
เปลี่ยนชื่อไฟล์ DLL ของคนร้ายให้ตรงกับชื่อไฟล์ของโปรแกรมที่ถูกต้องเพื่อทำ DLL Side-Loading

hyde.name: Masquerading
hyde.description: Adversaries may disguise scripts by assigning them misleading file extensions associated with ordinary data files. This can help evade attention and hinder detection based on file type.

hyde.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
hyde.description: Adversaries may decode obfuscated scripts or payloads during execution to recover executable code or commands. This can conceal malicious content from static analysis and security tools.

hyde.name: PowerShell
hyde.description: Adversaries may use PowerShell to execute additional scripts or payloads, including scripts that have been obfuscated or decoded at runtime. PowerShell provides access to system functions and can facilitate follow-on actions.

hyde.name: DLL Side-Loading
hyde.description: Adversaries may place a malicious DLL where a legitimate application will load it instead of the intended library. This abuses the application’s DLL search order to execute malicious code under the context of a trusted process.

hyde.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
hyde.description: Adversaries may obfuscate PowerShell commands and script content to conceal their behavior, including communications with command and control infrastructure. Obfuscation can hinder analysis and reduce the effectiveness of signature-based detection.

hyde.name: Match Legitimate Name or Location
hyde.description: Adversaries may name malicious DLLs to match legitimate libraries expected by trusted applications. This can support DLL side-loading and make malicious files appear legitimate during execution or review.

sub_queries: อีเมล Phishing แนบไฟล์เอกสารอันตรายหลอกนักวิจัยให้เปิดไฟล์แนบ
อีเมล Spearphishing Link อ้างเป็นการแจ้งเตือนความปลอดภัยของบัญชีและแนบลิงก์
ดัดแปลงเว็บไซต์ที่กลุ่มเป้าหมายเข้าใช้ประจำให้ติดตั้งโปรแกรมลงในเครื่องผู้เข้าชม (Drive-by Compromise)
แจกจ่ายโปรแกรมอันตรายผ่านเว็บไซต์แบ่งปันไฟล์
หลอกผู้เสียหายให้ติดตั้งส่วนขยายโปรแกรมท่องเว็บที่คนร้ายสร้างขึ้นเพื่อแทรกกลางการใช้งาน
ใช้ mshta.exe ดาวน์โหลดและสั่งรันไฟล์ HTML Application จากเครื่องปลายทางภายนอก (Signed Binary Proxy Execution: Mshta)

hyde.name: Spearphishing Attachment
hyde.description: Adversaries may send targeted emails containing malicious attachments designed to appear legitimate or relevant to the recipient. Opening the attachment may execute code, deliver malware, or enable follow-on activity.

hyde.name: Spearphishing Link
hyde.description: Adversaries may send targeted emails containing links to malicious or compromised websites, often using account or security notifications as lures. Recipients may be directed to download malware, provide credentials, or execute attacker-controlled content.

hyde.name: Drive-by Compromise
hyde.description: Adversaries may compromise websites frequently visited by a target audience and place malicious content or links on them. When users visit the site, their systems may be exploited or prompted to download and install malicious software.

hyde.name: Upload Malware
hyde.description: Adversaries may upload malicious files to third-party file-sharing services or other publicly accessible repositories. These services can be used to host and distribute malware or provide download locations for victims.

hyde.name: Browser Extensions
hyde.description: Adversaries may create or abuse browser extensions and persuade users to install them. Malicious extensions can monitor browsing activity, modify web content, intercept communications, or facilitate adversary-in-the-middle activity.

hyde.name: Mshta
hyde.description: Adversaries may abuse mshta.exe, a trusted Windows utility, to execute HTML Applications or script-based content. The utility may retrieve content from a remote location and execute it to bypass application controls or proxy malicious activity through a signed binary.

sub_queries: เข้าถึงเครื่องแม่ข่ายผ่านบริการ RDP ที่เปิดให้เข้าถึงจากอินเทอร์เน็ตและใช้รหัสผ่านที่คาดเดาได้
ส่งอีเมล Phishing และอีเมลขยะจำนวนมากพร้อมไฟล์แนบโปรแกรมเรียกค่าไถ่ให้พนักงาน
ใช้ไฟล์แบตช์เรียกใช้สคริปต์ PowerShell เพื่อสั่งงานบนเครื่องผู้เสียหาย
โหลดโปรแกรมเรียกค่าไถ่เข้าไปทำงานในหน่วยความจำโดยไม่เขียนไฟล์ลงดิสก์ (fileless execution)
เข้ารหัสลับไฟล์งานในเครื่องแม่ข่ายและแสดงข้อความเรียกค่าไถ่ (ransomware impact)

hyde.name: Remote Desktop Protocol
hyde.description: Adversaries may use Remote Desktop Protocol to access systems remotely, particularly when the service is exposed to the internet and protected by weak or guessable credentials. This access can enable interactive control of compromised hosts and facilitate subsequent intrusion activities.

hyde.name: Spearphishing Attachment
hyde.description: Adversaries may send phishing messages containing malicious attachments, including executable payloads, to trick recipients into opening or running them. Such messages may be distributed broadly or targeted to specific users to obtain initial execution.

hyde.name: PowerShell
hyde.description: Adversaries may use PowerShell scripts invoked through batch files to execute commands and automate actions on compromised systems. PowerShell can be used to download, configure, or launch additional malicious payloads.

hyde.name: Reflective Code Loading
hyde.description: Adversaries may load executable code directly into process memory without writing the payload to disk. This can reduce the presence of artifacts on the file system and help evade file-based security controls.

hyde.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt data on local or network-accessible systems to disrupt availability and impede normal operations. They may display ransom notes or other demands in an attempt to pressure victims into providing payment.

sub_queries: ส่งคำสั่งระบบ Unix จากหมายเลขไอพีเดียวกันเพื่อประมวลผลบนเครื่องแม่ข่าย (Unix Shell)
เปิดอ่านไฟล์รายชื่อบัญชีผู้ใช้ของระบบเพื่อรวบรวมข้อมูลบัญชี (Account Discovery)
เปิดอ่านไฟล์ที่เก็บค่ารหัสผ่านของระบบเพื่อขโมยข้อมูลรับรอง (Password Policy/Stored Credentials)
เปลี่ยนสิทธิ์การเข้าถึงไฟล์ที่ซ่อนไว้ในโฟลเดอร์ไฟล์ชั่วคราว (File and Directory Permissions Modification)
เข้ารหัสคำสั่งและผลลัพธ์ที่รับส่งด้วยกุญแจลับเพื่อหลบเลี่ยงการตรวจจับ (Encrypted Channel)
ดาวน์โหลดโปรแกรมสำหรับเปิดช่องทางส่งต่อการเชื่อมต่อแบบย้อนกลับมายังเครื่องแม่ข่าย (Ingress Tool Transfer)
เปิดช่องทางเชื่อมต่อแบบย้อนกลับเพื่อเข้าถึงเครือข่ายภายในจากภายนอก (Proxy)

hyde.name: Unix Shell
hyde.description: Adversaries may execute commands through Unix shells to interact with systems and perform actions using native command-line utilities. This may be used to conduct discovery, modify system resources, or execute additional tools.

hyde.name: Account Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may attempt to identify accounts managed by the operating system. Account information can help adversaries determine valid users, understand system access, and select targets for further activity.

hyde.name: Credentials from Password Stores
hyde.description: Adversaries may access files or other local stores containing password information and other authentication data. This information may be used to obtain valid accounts, authenticate to systems, or escalate privileges.

hyde.name: File and Directory Permissions Modification
hyde.description: Adversaries may modify permissions or access control settings on files and directories. This can enable unauthorized access, facilitate execution, or help conceal malicious files.

hyde.name: Encrypted Channel
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt command, control, and other network traffic using symmetric or asymmetric cryptographic methods. Encryption can protect the confidentiality of communications and hinder network-based detection and analysis.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may transfer tools or files from an external system into a compromised environment. These tools may be used to establish persistence, enable remote access, or support subsequent actions.

hyde.name: Proxy
hyde.description: Adversaries may use an intermediary system or connection to relay traffic between a compromised host and an external destination. This can provide access to otherwise unreachable networks and help conceal the source or destination of communications.

hyde.description: Adversaries may download and store additional malware or implant installers on compromised systems. They may stage these files for later execution or deployment to other hosts.

hyde.name: Pass the Hash
hyde.description: Adversaries may use stolen password hashes to authenticate to remote systems without knowing the corresponding plaintext passwords. This technique can enable lateral movement and access to resources using valid account privileges.

hyde.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may copy tools, malware, or other files from one system to another over a network. They may transfer these files to stage payloads for execution on remote systems.

hyde.name: Remote Services
hyde.description: Adversaries may use remote services or administration mechanisms to execute programs and commands on another system. They may leverage these services to deploy and run malware remotely while using existing accounts or remote access tools.

hyde.name: Scheduled Task
hyde.description: Adversaries may configure scheduled tasks to launch malicious programs whenever a user logs on. This enables recurring execution without requiring the adversary to manually start the program.

hyde.name: System Owner/User Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may gather information about the system owner and the username of the currently logged-on user. This information may be used to identify the active account and tailor subsequent activity.

hyde.name: System Information Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may collect identifying information about a host, such as its machine name, operating system, hardware, or other system characteristics. This information may be used to profile the environment and determine how to proceed.

hyde.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt collected information with a key embedded in malicious software before transmission. Encrypting the data can conceal its contents and make analysis or detection more difficult.

hyde.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
hyde.description: Adversaries may exfiltrate collected information through an established command and control channel. Using the existing channel can blend the transfer with normal malicious communications and reduce the need for separate infrastructure.

hyde.name: Proxy
hyde.description: Adversaries may route network traffic through a compromised internal system that acts as an intermediary between an external source and a target. This can help conceal the origin of connections and bypass network access controls.

hyde.name: File Deletion
hyde.description: Adversaries may delete files, including tools, scripts, and generated output, from compromised systems to remove evidence of their activity. This can hinder forensic analysis and reduce the likelihood of detection.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may download tools or software to a compromised system from an external location. These tools may support remote access, execution, tunneling, or other follow-on activities.

hyde.name: Protocol Tunneling
hyde.description: Adversaries may encapsulate remote access traffic within another communication channel or protocol. This can obscure the underlying traffic and help evade network monitoring and security controls.

hyde.name: Valid Accounts
hyde.description: Adversaries may use previously obtained legitimate credentials, including domain administrator credentials, to access systems remotely. This enables them to blend in with normal authentication activity and operate with the privileges assigned to the compromised account.

hyde.name: Scheduled Task
hyde.description: Adversaries may modify existing scheduled tasks to execute malicious commands or programs. They may alter task actions, triggers, or configuration to establish persistence or run code with elevated privileges.

hyde.name: Scheduled Task
hyde.description: Adversaries may trigger a modified scheduled task to execute immediately rather than waiting for its normal schedule. This allows them to rapidly run malicious commands or payloads using the task's configured privileges.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may transfer and install malicious tools or implants on a compromised system. They may use the implant to establish continued access, execute commands, or perform discovery activities.

hyde.name: Domain Groups
hyde.description: Adversaries may enumerate membership in domain groups to identify accounts with elevated or administrative privileges. This information can help them select targets for credential theft, lateral movement, or privilege escalation.

hyde.name: Remote System Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may enumerate computers registered in a domain or otherwise accessible within an environment. This helps them identify potential targets for lateral movement, data collection, or further reconnaissance.

hyde.name: Phishing
hyde.description: Adversaries may send phishing emails designed to deceive recipients into disclosing information or performing actions that support unauthorized access. They may impersonate trusted entities or use urgent and convincing messages to increase the likelihood of user interaction.

hyde.name: Valid Accounts
hyde.description: Adversaries may use legitimate usernames and passwords obtained through theft, compromise, or other means to authenticate to remote services such as VPNs. Using valid accounts can help adversaries bypass some access controls and blend in with normal user activity.

hyde.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
hyde.description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in authentication protocols or other system components to obtain higher-level privileges. Successful exploitation can allow them to gain administrative access and perform actions restricted from lower-privileged accounts.

hyde.name: Remote Desktop Protocol
hyde.description: Adversaries may use Remote Desktop Protocol to connect to and control remote systems within a network. They may use these sessions to move laterally, execute commands, access resources, or expand their foothold.

hyde.name: External Remote Services
hyde.description: Adversaries may establish or maintain access to internal networks through externally accessible remote services such as VPNs. They may keep these connections available for continued access while avoiding the need to repeatedly compromise internal systems.

hyde.name: PowerShell
hyde.description: Adversaries may use PowerShell to execute commands, run scripts, and automate actions on Windows systems. PowerShell can enable execution of payloads, system discovery, credential access, and other activities while using a tool commonly present on the operating system.

hyde.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt data on targeted systems to disrupt availability and prevent users from accessing files or services. They may encrypt local or network-accessible data and use the disruption to extort victims or impede business operations.

hyde.name: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
hyde.description: Adversaries may transfer collected data to cloud storage accounts or services under their control using file-transfer tools or web-based interfaces. This enables them to move data outside the compromised environment for later use, sale, or extortion.

hyde.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt files using a combination of symmetric and public-key cryptography to make data inaccessible without a decryption key. They may use hybrid encryption to efficiently process large amounts of data while protecting the key needed for recovery.

hyde.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt only portions of files or alternate encrypted and unencrypted sections to accelerate encryption and reduce the likelihood of detection. This can render files unusable while limiting the processing time and system activity associated with the attack.

hyde.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt data on systems or network shares to interrupt access to business operations and coerce victims into paying a ransom. They may deploy ransomware broadly across endpoints and servers to maximize the operational impact.

hyde.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
hyde.description: Adversaries may threaten to publicly release stolen data in addition to encrypting systems, using the risk of disclosure to increase pressure for payment. This double-extortion approach combines operational disruption with the potential exposure of sensitive information.

hyde.name: Logon Scripts
hyde.description: Adversaries may configure logon scripts to execute commands or programs automatically when a user logs on. This can establish persistence and ensure malicious code runs in the context of the user session.

hyde.name: Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription
hyde.description: Adversaries may create WMI event subscriptions that trigger commands when specified system conditions occur, such as a particular time or event. This can provide fileless persistence by invoking malicious code through WMI without requiring an executable to remain on disk.

hyde.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
hyde.description: Adversaries may add entries to registry Run keys to launch programs automatically when a user logs on or the system starts. This can establish persistence and cause malicious software to execute repeatedly without requiring user interaction.

hyde.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
hyde.description: Adversaries may place malicious programs or shortcuts in startup folders so they are executed automatically during system or user startup. This can establish persistence by causing the programs to run whenever the relevant user session begins.

hyde.name: Remote Access Software
hyde.description: Adversaries may deploy remote access software on a compromised system to control it remotely. Such software can provide interactive access, execute commands, and support persistence or follow-on operations.

hyde.name: Scheduled Task/Job
hyde.description: Adversaries may create scheduled tasks that masquerade as legitimate system or maintenance activities to execute malicious programs at recurring intervals. Scheduled execution can establish persistence and ensure that payloads run periodically without user interaction.

hyde.name: External Proxy
hyde.description: Adversaries may route command and control traffic through a compromised system acting as an intermediary between external infrastructure and other connections. This can obscure the origin of communications and help bypass network access controls.

hyde.name: Internal Proxy
hyde.description: Adversaries may use a compromised system as an intermediary to relay connections to other hosts within an internal network. This enables access to otherwise unreachable systems and facilitates lateral movement or deeper network penetration.

hyde.name: Symmetric Cryptography
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt command and control traffic in both directions using a shared secret key, including strong symmetric algorithms. Encrypted communications can conceal transferred data and commands from network monitoring and inspection tools.

hyde.name: System Name Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may query the hostname or other system naming information to identify the computer on which they are operating. This information may support host tracking, targeting, and discovery of additional systems.

hyde.name: System Owner/User Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may enumerate the username or account associated with the current session. This information may help identify the privileges, role, or identity context available on the compromised system.

hyde.name: System Name Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may query the hostname again after accessing another system to confirm the identity of the current host. This may help track movement across systems and prevent confusion during reconnaissance.

hyde.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may inspect network configuration details such as IP addresses, gateways, and DNS servers. This information may be used to understand network topology, identify reachable systems, and plan further operations.

hyde.name: Account Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may use command-line utilities or other operating system functions to enumerate user accounts in a domain. This information may help identify valid accounts, privileged users, and potential targets for further access.

hyde.name: Permission Groups Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may enumerate domain groups and inspect their memberships, including groups associated with administrative privileges. This information may be used to identify accounts with elevated permissions and opportunities for privilege escalation or lateral movement.

hyde.name: Password Policy Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may query domain password policies to determine requirements such as minimum password length and account lockout thresholds. This information may help them select credential attack methods while reducing the likelihood of detection or account lockout.

hyde.name: Spearphishing Attachment
hyde.description: Adversaries may send malicious files as email attachments to entice recipients to open them. These attachments may exploit user interaction to execute code and establish control of the targeted system.

hyde.name: Right-to-Left Override
hyde.description: Adversaries may insert a Right-to-Left Override character into a filename to manipulate the displayed order of characters. This can make an executable file appear to have a benign document extension and deceive users into opening it.

hyde.name: PowerShell
hyde.description: Adversaries may use PowerShell to execute commands, scripts, and other payloads on a system. PowerShell may be launched from a command shell to perform system execution and support follow-on attack activity.

hyde.name: Automated Collection
hyde.description: Adversaries may use scripts or commands to automatically search for and collect files matching specified names, extensions, or other criteria. Automated collection enables adversaries to gather targeted data efficiently before staging or exfiltration.

hyde.name: Archive Collected Data
hyde.description: Adversaries may compress collected files into an archive using operating system utilities or other available tools. Archiving combines data into fewer files and may reduce its size to facilitate staging and exfiltration.

เปิดอ่านไฟล์ผลลัพธ์ที่โปรแกรมดักบันทึกแป้นพิมพ์จัดเก็บไว้
อัปโหลดโปรแกรมเพื่อดึงชื่อผู้ใช้และรหัสผ่านที่โปรแกรมท่องเว็บบันทึกไว้ในเครื่อง (Credentials from Web Browsers)

ลบไฟล์ที่เกี่ยวข้องกับโปรแกรมดักบันทึกแป้นพิมพ์ในโฟลเดอร์ไฟล์ชั่วคราว (File and Directory Discovery)

hyde.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
hyde.description: Adversaries may add commands or scripts to Windows Registry run keys or startup folders to execute programs automatically when a user logs on. This persistence mechanism allows malicious code to run under the context of the logged-on user without requiring manual execution.

hyde.name: Keylogging
hyde.description: Adversaries may capture user keystrokes by deploying keylogging software and executing it with the privileges of the targeted user. Keylogging can enable the collection of credentials, sensitive communications, and other information entered through the keyboard.

hyde.name: Data from Local System
hyde.description: Adversaries may read files stored on a compromised system to collect locally generated information, such as logs or captured input. This data may be accessed to obtain credentials, sensitive content, or other information useful for further operations.

hyde.name: Credentials from Web Browsers
hyde.description: Adversaries may extract usernames, passwords, and other authentication data stored by web browsers on a compromised system. Browser credential stores may be accessed with dedicated tools or scripts to obtain credentials for accessing additional systems and services.

hyde.name: Indicator Removal on Host
hyde.description: Adversaries may stop malicious processes after completing collection activities to reduce the likelihood of detection and limit further execution. Terminating associated programs can also support cleanup and removal of active components from the compromised system.

hyde.name: File Deletion
hyde.description: Adversaries may delete files associated with malicious tools, including artifacts stored in temporary directories, after completing their activities. File deletion can remove evidence of execution and hinder forensic analysis or incident response.

คัดลอกสำเนาโปรแกรมอันตรายไปยังสื่อบันทึกแบบถอดได้
คัดลอกสำเนาโปรแกรมอันตรายไปยังโฟลเดอร์ที่เปิดแบ่งปันบนเครือข่าย

hyde.name: Malicious File
hyde.description: Adversaries may deliver malicious files to a system and cause them to be opened or executed, resulting in the installation of unwanted or harmful software. They may use executable files, scripts, documents, or other file types to establish an initial foothold.

hyde.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
hyde.description: Adversaries may use a backdoor to receive and execute commands on compromised systems. This enables them to perform follow-on actions and control system behavior remotely.

hyde.name: System Information Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may gather information about a compromised system, such as its operating system, hostname, hardware, and configuration. This information can help them identify the environment and select appropriate follow-on actions.

hyde.name: Application Layer Protocol
hyde.description: Adversaries may communicate with command and control infrastructure using application-layer protocols. Such communications can allow compromised systems to check in, receive instructions, and send collected information.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may download additional tools, payloads, or components from command and control infrastructure to a compromised system. They may then install or execute the transferred files to expand functionality or support follow-on activity.

hyde.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
hyde.description: Adversaries may exploit vulnerabilities in remote services on other systems to spread malware or gain access to additional devices. This can allow propagation without requiring direct user interaction on each targeted system.

hyde.name: Replication Through Removable Media
hyde.description: Adversaries may copy malicious files to removable media and use that media to spread malware to other systems. They may rely on users or automated processes to access the media and execute the copied files.

hyde.name: Taint Shared Content
hyde.description: Adversaries may place malicious files in shared folders or other commonly accessed network locations. Users or systems that access the shared content may then execute the files, enabling malware propagation.

โปรแกรมฝังตัวดาวน์โหลดไฟล์โปรแกรมหลัก ไฟล์ประกอบ สคริปต์ติดตั้ง ไฟล์กฎการคัดกรองจดหมาย และไฟล์ตั้งค่าเข้ามาเก็บไว้

hyde.name: Email Collection
hyde.description: Adversaries may access and collect email messages from user mailboxes or local email stores. They may target sensitive communications to obtain information for intelligence gathering or further compromise.

hyde.name: Email Forwarding Rule
hyde.description: Adversaries may create or modify email forwarding rules to automatically send messages to an account they control. They may use this capability to collect incoming and outgoing communications while reducing the need for direct mailbox access.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may download tools, payloads, scripts, configuration files, and other supporting components onto a compromised system. They may stage these files locally to prepare for execution, installation, or further operations.

hyde.name: Valid Accounts
hyde.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse legitimate account credentials, including privileged domain accounts, to access systems and resources. Using valid accounts can allow adversaries to bypass access controls and blend their activity with legitimate user behavior.

hyde.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may copy tools, payloads, scripts, and configuration files from a compromised system to another system in the environment. They may transfer these files to stage or deploy malicious software on a targeted host.

hyde.name: Remote Services
hyde.description: Adversaries may use remote services or remote administration mechanisms to execute commands and install software on another system. They may leverage these capabilities to deploy and operate malicious components without requiring physical access to the target host.

hyde.name: Transport Agent
hyde.description: Adversaries may install or modify a mail transport component that executes within the server’s message-processing pipeline. They may use this component to intercept, alter, redirect, or collect email messages as they pass through the server.

hyde.name: Cron
hyde.description: Adversaries may create or modify cron jobs to execute malicious programs or commands at recurring intervals. They may use scheduled execution to maintain persistence or repeatedly perform actions on a compromised system.

hyde.name: Systemd Service
hyde.description: Adversaries may create or modify systemd service units to execute malicious programs or commands automatically when a system starts. They may use these services to establish persistence and run code with the privileges assigned to the service.

hyde.name: /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow
hyde.description: Adversaries may read Linux account files containing user account information and password hashes. They may attempt to obtain password hashes for offline cracking or to identify accounts that can be targeted for further access.

hyde.name: Bash History
hyde.description: Adversaries may read shell history files to obtain previously executed commands and potentially recover credentials, sensitive information, or details about administrative activity. They may use this information to discover commands, files, systems, and services of interest.

hyde.name: Private Keys
hyde.description: Adversaries may search for and read private keys stored on compromised systems. They may use obtained keys to authenticate to remote systems, access protected resources, or maintain access without using passwords.

ใช้ช่องโหว่อีกรายการเพื่อยกระดับสิทธิ์ให้สคริปต์ทำงานด้วยสิทธิ์สูงสุดของระบบ
ใช้ส่วนประกอบสร้างข้อความแจ้งเตือนของซอฟต์แวร์ที่ติดตั้งอยู่แล้วส่งคำขอผ่านโพรโทคอลเว็บเพื่อสั่งงานเครื่องที่ยึดครองไว้

hyde.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
hyde.description: Adversaries may exploit vulnerabilities in applications, services, or systems that are accessible from the internet. They may use crafted requests or commands to gain unauthorized access or execute code on the targeted system.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may transfer malicious files, scripts, or tools from an external system to a compromised environment. They may use web requests or other network mechanisms to retrieve payloads needed for execution or further activity.

hyde.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
hyde.description: Adversaries may execute commands or scripts through an available command interpreter on a compromised system. They may use scripting capabilities to automate actions, run payloads, or perform follow-on operations.

hyde.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
hyde.description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities to obtain higher-level permissions than those initially available. They may use these elevated privileges to execute code, access protected resources, or control system functions.

hyde.name: Web Protocols
hyde.description: Adversaries may use HTTP or HTTPS communications to send commands to and receive information from compromised systems. They may abuse legitimate software components that generate web-based requests so that command-and-control traffic blends with normal application activity.

อัปโหลดไฟล์โปรแกรมขนาดเล็กไปยังเครื่องแม่ข่ายควบคุมโดเมนและสั่งให้ทำงาน
ติดต่อกลับไปยังเครื่องสั่งการภายนอกผ่านหมายเลขพอร์ตที่ไม่ใช่พอร์ตมาตรฐานเพื่อหลีกเลี่ยงการตรวจจับ
สอบถามระบบทะเบียนโดเมนเพื่อค้นหารายละเอียดเครื่องคอมพิวเตอร์ที่ผู้บริหารฝ่ายการเงินใช้งานอยู่

hyde.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may query domain naming services to resolve hostnames into IP addresses. This information can help identify networked systems and select additional targets for follow-on activity.

hyde.name: Service Execution
hyde.description: Adversaries may create or manipulate a system service on a remote host to execute commands or payloads. This can enable remote execution from a previously compromised system while blending activity with legitimate service operations.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may upload executable files, scripts, or other tools to a compromised system. They may then execute the transferred content to extend capabilities, perform actions, or establish access.

hyde.name: Non-Standard Port
hyde.description: Adversaries may communicate with external command and control infrastructure over ports that are not normally associated with the selected protocol or service. Using atypical ports can help evade network monitoring and filtering based on expected service behavior.

hyde.name: Remote System Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may query domain services or other network resources to identify remote computers and associated system details. This information can help locate systems used by specific users or groups and guide subsequent targeting.

sub_queries: แก้ไขซอฟต์แวร์ระดับเฟิร์มแวร์ที่ฝังอยู่ในอุปกรณ์เราเตอร์หลายเครื่อง

เปิดช่องทางเชื่อมต่อระยะไกลลับเพื่อให้คนร้ายเข้าถึงอุปกรณ์เราเตอร์ได้ตลอดเวลา
ซ่อนการเชื่อมต่อระยะไกลของคนร้ายไม่ให้ถูกบันทึกในไฟล์บันทึกเหตุการณ์ของอุปกรณ์
ใช้แพ็กเก็ตที่ประกอบขึ้นเป็นพิเศษเพื่อเปิดและปิดช่องทางลับบนอุปกรณ์เราเตอร์ (Traffic Signaling)

hyde.name: Modify System Image
hyde.description: Adversaries may modify system images, including firmware or other software images, to insert malicious code or alter system behavior. This can provide persistence and control at a level that is difficult to detect or remediate through normal software administration.

hyde.name: System Firmware
hyde.description: Adversaries may implant malicious code into system firmware to execute below the operating system and maintain persistence across reboots or system updates. Firmware implants can provide continued access while evading security controls operating at higher layers.

hyde.name: External Remote Services
hyde.description: Adversaries may enable or abuse remote services to establish persistent access to network devices or other systems. They may conceal or restrict the service to authorized users or specific conditions to maintain access while reducing the likelihood of discovery.

hyde.name: Indicator Blocking
hyde.description: Adversaries may prevent security-relevant activity from being recorded or transmitted to monitoring systems. Blocking logs or other indicators can conceal remote access and hinder detection and investigation.

hyde.name: Traffic Signaling
hyde.description: Adversaries may use specially crafted network traffic to signal a compromised system to activate or deactivate a capability. This can keep a backdoor inactive during normal operation and reduce the likelihood that it will be discovered by network monitoring.

อาศัยความสัมพันธ์ความน่าเชื่อถือระหว่างโดเมนบริษัทลูกกับสำนักงานใหญ่เพื่อข้ามเครือข่ายเข้ามา (Trusted Relationship)
ขโมยใบรับรองสำหรับลงลายมือชื่อโปรแกรมมาเซ็นกำกับไฟล์โปรแกรมอันตรายให้ดูเหมือนซอฟต์แวร์ถูกต้อง (Code Signing Certificates)
เปิดเชลล์รับการเชื่อมต่อค้างไว้เพื่อคงอยู่ในเครื่องผู้เสียหาย
แก้ไขทะเบียนระบบเพื่อเปิดใช้งาน Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP)
คงอยู่และเข้าใช้งานเครื่องผ่าน SSH

hyde.name: Disable or Modify System Logging
hyde.description: Adversaries may disable or modify system logging to prevent events from being recorded or to reduce the visibility of their activities. This can hinder detection, analysis, and forensic investigation of malicious behavior.

hyde.name: Trusted Relationship
hyde.description: Adversaries may exploit established trust relationships between organizations, domains, or networks to gain access to additional systems. This may allow them to move between environments without directly compromising each target.

hyde.name: Code Signing Certificates
hyde.description: Adversaries may obtain or steal code-signing certificates and use them to sign malicious files. Signed files may appear legitimate and evade security controls that rely on signature validation or user trust.

hyde.name: Web Shell
hyde.description: Adversaries may install or maintain a shell on a compromised system that accepts remote connections or commands. This provides persistent access and enables adversaries to execute actions while blending their activity with legitimate server functionality.

hyde.name: Modify Registry
hyde.description: Adversaries may modify the Windows Registry to change system configuration, enable functionality, or establish persistence. Registry changes may be used to enable remote access services such as Remote Desktop Protocol.

hyde.name: SSH
hyde.description: Adversaries may use Secure Shell to remotely access and control systems using valid credentials or previously established access. SSH provides encrypted command execution and file transfer capabilities that can support persistence, lateral movement, and remote administration.

เปลี่ยนนามสกุลของไฟล์ที่เข้ารหัสแล้วทุกไฟล์เป็นนามสกุลเฉพาะของโปรแกรมเรียกค่าไถ่
ใช้ PowerShell ลบไฟล์โปรแกรมเรียกค่าไถ่ออกจากเครือข่ายผ่านหน้าต่างคำสั่งที่ซ่อนไม่ให้ผู้ใช้มองเห็น
สำรวจเครือข่ายของโรงพยาบาล
เข้ารหัสข้อมูลของโรงพยาบาลด้วยกุญแจสาธารณะขนาด 4096 บิตร่วมกับอัลกอริทึมเข้ารหัสแบบสตรีม
นำข้อมูลอ่อนไหวของโรงพยาบาลออกไปเพื่อข่มขู่ว่าจะเผยแพร่ (Exfiltration)
เรียกค่าไถ่แลกกับการถอดรหัสข้อมูลและไม่เผยแพร่ข้อมูลอ่อนไหว โดยให้โอนเงินสกุลเงินดิจิทัลไปยังกระเป๋าเงินที่กำหนด

hyde.name: Process Injection
hyde.description: Adversaries may insert malicious code into the memory space of a running process. They may do so to execute code under another process’s context, evade defenses, or inherit the process’s permissions.

hyde.name: Modify Registry
hyde.description: Adversaries may modify the Windows Registry using command-line utilities or other system interfaces. They may alter configuration settings to establish persistence, weaken security controls, or change system behavior.

hyde.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt files and rename them with a distinctive extension associated with the attack. They may do so to prevent access to data and signal that the files have been affected by ransomware.

hyde.name: File Deletion
hyde.description: Adversaries may delete files associated with their tools or payloads after execution, including by invoking PowerShell through a hidden command window. They may do so to remove forensic artifacts and hinder detection or analysis.

hyde.name: Network Service Scanning
hyde.description: Adversaries may scan networks to identify hosts, services, and accessible systems. They may use the results to map the environment, locate valuable resources, and select targets for further activity.

hyde.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt data using asymmetric keys together with symmetric or stream-cipher algorithms. They may do so to deny access to files and demand payment for recovery.

hyde.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
hyde.description: Adversaries may transfer sensitive data from compromised environments to infrastructure under their control, including through command-and-control channels. They may use the stolen information for espionage, coercion, public disclosure, or extortion.

hyde.name: Financial Theft
hyde.description: Adversaries may demand payment from victims in exchange for restoring access to encrypted data or withholding stolen information. They may request cryptocurrency transfers to specified wallets to facilitate collection and complicate attribution.

sub_queries: โปรแกรมไม่พึงประสงค์แทรกในเว็บเบราว์เซอร์เพื่อดักจับและแก้ไขข้อมูลที่ผู้ใช้กรอกบนหน้าเว็บธนาคาร (Web Portal Capture)
ขโมยชื่อผู้ใช้และรหัสผ่านของผู้เสียหายจากข้อมูลที่กรอกบนเว็บไซต์ธนาคาร (Credentials from Web Browsers)
ดาวน์โหลดไฟล์โปรแกรมอันตรายเพิ่มเติมจากเครื่องภายนอกแล้วติดตั้งบนเครื่องผู้เสียหาย (Ingress Tool Transfer)
ส่งข้อมูลที่รวบรวมได้ไปยังเครื่องสั่งการที่กำหนดไว้ตายตัวผ่านช่องทาง C2 (Exfiltration Over C2 Channel)
แอบใช้ทรัพยากรเครื่องผู้เสียหายขุดเหรียญสกุลเงินดิจิทัล (Resource Hijacking)
เรียกดูข้อมูลระบบของเครื่องผู้เสียหาย (System Information Discovery)
เรียกดูข้อมูลเฟิร์มแวร์ระดับล่างของเครื่องผู้เสียหาย (System Firmware Discovery)

hyde.name: Web Portal Capture
hyde.description: Adversaries may capture credentials and other sensitive information entered into web portals by injecting or modifying browser content. This technique can be used to intercept data before it is encrypted and transmitted to the legitimate service.

hyde.name: Credentials from Web Browsers
hyde.description: Adversaries may search web browsers for stored credentials, including usernames, passwords, cookies, and other authentication data. This information may be collected from browser databases, configuration files, or credential storage mechanisms for account access.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
hyde.description: Adversaries may download tools or other files into a compromised environment from external systems. The transferred files may be used to install additional malware, execute follow-on actions, or expand access.

hyde.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
hyde.description: Adversaries may exfiltrate collected data over an existing command and control channel. Using the C2 channel can help conceal the transfer and reduce the need for separate exfiltration infrastructure.

hyde.name: Resource Hijacking
hyde.description: Adversaries may use the computing resources of compromised systems to perform resource-intensive activities such as cryptocurrency mining. This activity can degrade system performance and generate illicit revenue for the adversary.

hyde.name: System Information Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may gather information about operating systems, hardware, software, and other system characteristics. This information can help identify targets, select appropriate tools, and guide subsequent actions.

hyde.name: System Firmware Discovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may query system firmware and related low-level hardware information. This information can be used to identify system configurations, assess persistence opportunities, or support targeting decisions.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer

hyde.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
hyde.description: Adversaries may execute downloaded programs through commands issued within a remote session. They may use command interpreters or scripts to launch tools, automate actions, and execute additional payloads.

hyde.name: System Information Discovery

hyde.name: Software Discovery

hyde.name: Account Discovery

hyde.name: System Network Configuration Discovery

hyde.name: Input Capture
hyde.description: Adversaries may record user keystrokes to capture sensitive information such as credentials, messages, and commands. Keylogging may be implemented through malware, hooks, or other mechanisms that monitor keyboard input.

hyde.name: Ingress Tool Transfer

hyde.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
hyde.description: Adversaries may use command interpreters or scripting mechanisms to launch additional files on a compromised host. This enables execution of transferred payloads and other tools needed to maintain or expand access.

hyde.name: Remote Access Software
hyde.description: Adversaries may use remote access software to interact with a compromised system as if operating it directly. Such software can provide visibility into the target's screen and enable remote control for executing actions and manipulating the host.

hyde.name: Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol

hyde.name: Domain Account

hyde.name: Domain Groups

hyde.name: System Network Configuration Discovery

hyde.name: Inhibit System Recovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may stop services responsible for creating or maintaining recovery artifacts to prevent restoration of affected systems. They may do so before or during destructive actions to reduce the likelihood that data can be recovered.

hyde.name: Inhibit System Recovery
hyde.description: Adversaries may delete existing shadow copies and other recovery artifacts to prevent restoration of affected files or systems. This may be performed using native operating system utilities or other tools.

hyde.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
hyde.description: Adversaries may use command-line interfaces and scripts to execute commands that stop services and delete recovery artifacts. This enables them to automate actions and carry out system changes through native interpreters.

hyde.name: Clear Windows Event Logs
hyde.description: Adversaries may clear Windows event logs, including System, Security, and Application logs, to remove evidence of malicious activity. They may use native utilities, scripts, or APIs to erase selected or all recorded events.

hyde.name: Modify Registry
hyde.description: Adversaries may modify Windows Registry values to remove or alter security software signature databases. This can reduce the ability of defensive tools to identify known malicious files.

hyde.name: Impair Defenses
hyde.description: Adversaries may modify system settings, including Windows Registry values, to disable or weaken antivirus and other security software. This allows subsequent malicious activity to proceed with reduced detection or prevention.

hyde.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
hyde.description: Adversaries may exfiltrate data to online storage or other web services using file-copying utilities or similar tools. Web services can provide a convenient destination for transferring and storing stolen information outside the compromised environment.

hyde.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
hyde.description: Adversaries may encrypt data on targeted systems or network shares to interrupt availability and inhibit access to business information. They may use encryption keys controlled by the adversary and demand payment in exchange for restoration.

hyde.name: Ransom Note
hyde.description: Adversaries may place ransom notes in directories containing encrypted or otherwise affected files to communicate demands and threaten data loss. The notes may warn victims not to modify, rename, or delete files or keys needed for recovery.
